LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we read widely? 2. What materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,
2. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency,
3. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment,
4. realise the importance of independent reading in lifelong learning. The learner is guided to: narratives, poems, newspapers and magazines in print or electronic format, meet on a regular basis and read varied texts, collaboratively, texts they have read, extensively, pleasure. read widely? do you enjoy reading?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading.
2. Explain Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why should we read widely? 2. What materials do you enjoy reading?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

2. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency,
3. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment,
4. realise the importance of independent reading in lifelong learning.
